result:
I would close the gap between what is intellectually known and what feels real.

Human minds evolved for small groups and immediate horizons. If someone is hurting right in front of you, or if a threat is five minutes away, you feel it viscerally and act. But stretch that same reality across an ocean, a border, a screen, or fifty years into the future, and it turns into an abstraction—a statistic, a talking point, or someone else’s problem.

Almost every catastrophic failure in human history—wars, ecological collapse, systemic cruelty, the quiet neglect of preventable suffering—relies on that dilution. People are rarely willing to cause or ignore devastation when they can feel its full weight. They only manage it because distance and time act as an anesthetic.

If I could change one thing, I wouldn’t force agreement or take away human choice. I would simply make it impossible for distance, numbers, or time to make other lives feel less real than the one right in front of you.
